name: יְשִׂימִאֵל
summary: Jesimiel is one of the men of Simeon listed by name in 1Ch 4:34–37, “princes in their clans” (4:38), who in the days of Hezekiah went to the entrance of Gedor for pasture and struck the people living there (4:39–41). He is named once only. The name is the imperfect of שִׂים, יָשִׂים “he sets”, with אֵל “God”: “God sets” or “may God establish”, formed as יִשְׁמָעֵאל “God hears” is from שָׁמַע. Scripture does not explain it; the sense is the verb's “set, make, establish”, as when God says of Ishmael, “I will make him a great nation”.

evidence.note: “… and Asaiah and Adiel וִישִׂימִאֵל and Benaiah”: the only verse that names him.
“These who are mentioned by name were princes in their clans.”
“These written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah.”
The verb with God as subject: “a great nation אֲשִׂימֶנּוּ”.
יִשְׁמָעֵאל, the same pattern of name, explained in the text: “for Yahweh has heard”.

note: The lexicon lead prints the name with shin (יְשִׁימִאֵל); the text has sin, וִישִׂימִאֵל, and the name is given so here. Read as jussive, the name is a wish, “may God establish”; scripture gives no explanation of it, so the gloss rests on the form alone.
